Can you guarantee first position on Google?

We can commit to agreed work and transparent reporting, but we can’t guarantee a search ranking or a fixed number of leads. We’ll set measurable goals around your website and market. What outcome matters most to you?
What is robots.txt?

A robots.txt file gives cooperating crawlers instructions about which paths they may fetch. It is not a password system, and blocking crawling alone does not reliably remove a URL from search results. Would you like to know how this applies to your website?
What is XML sitemap?

An XML sitemap lists preferred public URLs to help search engines discover a site’s content. Submitting it supports discovery but does not guarantee that every URL will be indexed. Would you like to know how this applies to your website?
What is Schema?

Schema is a shared vocabulary for describing things such as an organization, article, or product in machine-readable data. Markup should describe the visible content accurately; it does not guarantee a special search appearance. Would you like to know how this applies to your website?
What is Canonical URL?

A canonical URL is the preferred address for a page among duplicate or very similar versions. A canonical annotation is a signal rather than an instruction that search engines must always follow. Would you like to know how this applies to your website?
What is Crawling?

Crawling is how a search engine fetches pages and follows links to discover content. A page must be reachable before its content can be evaluated for search, although crawling and indexing are different stages. Would you like to know how this applies to your website?
What is Indexing?

Indexing is the process of analyzing and storing information about a page so it may be considered for search results. Being indexed does not guarantee a particular position or traffic level. Would you like to know how this applies to your website?
What is Noindex?

Noindex tells supporting search engines not to include a page in their search index. The crawler generally needs access to the page to see this directive, so a robots.txt block can prevent it from being read. Would you like to know how this applies to your website?
What is Nofollow?

Nofollow is a link relationship value used to qualify a link’s relationship to its destination. It is different from noindex, which concerns whether a page should appear in a search index. Would you like to know how this applies to your website?

What is Backlink?

A backlink is a link from another website to yours. Relevance, context, and legitimacy matter; simply accumulating a large number of links is not a reliable strategy for useful visibility. Would you like to know how this applies to your website?
What is Anchor text?

Anchor text is the visible wording of a link. Descriptive wording helps people understand the destination, whereas repeated vague labels provide less context about what the linked page contains. Would you like to know how this applies to your website?
What is Internal link?

An internal link connects pages on the same website. Useful internal links help visitors navigate related information and help crawlers discover how the site’s pages relate to each other. Would you like to know how this applies to your website?
What is External link?

An external link points from your website to a different website. Link to relevant, trustworthy sources when they help the reader verify a claim or continue a useful task. Would you like to know how this applies to your website?
What is Keyword?

A keyword is a word or phrase used to describe a search topic or target an advertising opportunity. Good research considers the intent and business relevance behind a phrase rather than treating volume as the only criterion. Would you like to know how this applies to your website?
What is Search intent?

Search intent is the task or need behind a query, such as learning, comparing, finding a location, or buying. A useful page should fit that task instead of merely repeating the query’s words. Would you like to know how this applies to your website?
What is Long-tail keyword?

A long-tail keyword is a more specific search phrase within a broader topic. Specific phrases can reveal a clearer customer need, but they are not automatically easy to rank for or commercially valuable. Would you like to know how this applies to your website?
What is SERP?

SERP means search engine results page. Its layout can include organic links, ads, local results, images, and other features depending on the query and the search system. Would you like to know how this applies to your website?

What is API?

An API defines how software systems exchange requests and results. Reliable integrations validate inputs, handle failures, protect credentials, and report the actual outcome of an external action. Would you like to know how this applies to your website?
What is Webhook?

A webhook sends a notification to another system when an event occurs. Verify the sender, handle retries safely, and avoid creating duplicate actions when a notification is delivered more than once. Would you like to know how this applies to your website?
What is TLS?

TLS protects data in transit between appropriately configured endpoints. An SSL certificate is commonly used wording for the certificate involved, but transport encryption does not establish that every part of an application is secure. Would you like to know how this applies to your website?
What is HTTPS?

HTTPS is HTTP carried over a protected TLS connection. It helps protect traffic in transit, while application security still depends on access controls, updates, validation, and other implementation details. Would you like to know how this applies to your website?
What is DNS?

DNS publishes records that help systems locate services associated with a domain. Website routing, email delivery, and verification can use different record types and hostnames within the same domain. Would you like to know how this applies to your website?
What is CDN?

A content delivery network distributes eligible content through geographically distributed infrastructure. Correct caching and appropriately sized assets still matter; a CDN cannot automatically repair an oversized image or broken application. Would you like to know how this applies to your website?
What is Web hosting?

Web hosting provides the infrastructure needed to serve a website or application. The plan must support the framework, server features, storage, and deployment process the project actually uses. Would you like to know how this applies to your website?
What is Supabase?

Supabase provides database and related application services built around PostgreSQL. Protect server credentials, use appropriate access policies, and verify saved records independently of email notification delivery. Would you like to know how this applies to your website?
